title: Live Noise Fingerprints for Quantum Program Analysis
abstract: arXiv:2611.19143v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Quantum programs are probabilistic in nature, and noisy execution due to current imperfect hardware further complicates their analysis. In this paper, we study abstract semantics for analysing quantum programs under these conditions. We introduce noise fingerprints, compact descriptions of the observable effects of noise relative to a finite interface of input states and output measurements. We use them to define our abstract domain with respect to the concrete noise-related behaviour. We relate the concrete and abstract domains through a probabilistic Galois connection, extending the Galois-connection framework to distribution-valued interpretations. We study the resulting abstraction in terms of observational soundness, conciseness, efficiency, and ability to adapt to changing noise. translated_title: 量子程序分析中的实时噪声指纹
translated_abstract: 量子程序本质上是概率性的，而当前不完美硬件所导致的含噪执行进一步增加了其分析的难度。本文研究了在此类条件下分析量子程序的抽象语义。我们引入了“噪声指纹”的概念，即相对于有限的输入状态与输出测量接口，对噪声可观测效应的紧凑描述。我们利用噪声指纹来定义关于具体噪声相关行为的抽象域。我们通过概率伽罗瓦连接将具体域与抽象域关联起来，将伽罗瓦连接框架扩展到了以分布为取值的解释上。我们从观测可靠性、简洁性、效率以及适应噪声变化的能力等方面对所得的抽象进行了研究。我们证明，多项式规模的接口在保持所选观测结果的同时，能够产生比完整噪声模型指数级更小的指纹，并且……
tldr: 本文提出“噪声指纹”这一紧凑的抽象表示，并通过概率伽罗瓦连接将其与具体噪声行为关联，实现了对含噪量子程序的高效可靠分析，且多项式规模的接口可产生比完整噪声模型指数级更小的指纹。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "noise fingerprints" as compact abstract descriptions of noise effects on quantum programs, connected to concrete noise behavior via a probabilistic Galois connection, showing that polynomial-size interfaces yield exponentially smaller fingerprints than full noise models while preserving the chosen observations.
